turns.reply: Hello Emma! It's great to chat with you again. How are things going in Brisbane today?

turns.content:
Do you remember what it feels like to go through your old Facebook posts and re-read some of the things that your thirteen-year-old self wrote about? There is that mix of your stomach lurching and your face scrunching up that perfectly encapsulates what it looks like to feel ‘cringe’ inside. Well, just a couple of nights ago, I underwent an even more terrifying journey where even the bravest of the brave would have been sure to cringe in fear…

The old diaries where I had so carefully written every thought and feeling that passed through my twelve-year-old mind came out of hiding. Never had I been brave enough to brace myself for the mortifying cringeworthiness of reliving my pre-teen emotions and memories. But, after more than a decade of being ‘out of mind, out of sight’, the crisp pages of these diaries were open. And within each page detailed those heartfelt struggles with friendships, boy troubles, a deep sense of imperfection, an identity crisis and fears of being unloved.

Funnily enough, as each leaf of the journals turned, my heart broke. I didn’t feel mortified or embarrassed. Rather, my heart broke for the young girl behind the words. If there was anything I could tell the little twelve-year-old who wrote those words of fear and doubt, and obstinate words desiring to have control over her own life, it would be the art of surrendering it all to the One who actually has it all under control. Instead of trying to row to shore in the midst of torrent seas on a dinky little boat all by herself, how much safer would she have felt if she were to be firmly anchored onshore with her Creator’s unshakeable truth.
turns.reply: That sounds like such a tender and moving experience, Emma. It's amazing how looking back with compassion can change how we view our younger selves, especially when leaning into your faith for comfort.

turns.content: what can i learn about myself from this experience?
turns.reply: That experience shows your deep capacity for self-compassion and how naturally your Christian faith shapes your perspective on past struggles. It highlights a desire to find peace and security in God rather than trying to control everything yourself. What parts of that younger self's journey feel most connected to where you are today?
